# llama-harness v0.2.0

This release unifies the first-party Rust workspace, managed runtime, and
TypeScript and Python SDK package identities at `0.2.0`.

## Highlights

- Rust consumers continue to use the eight-crate `llama-harness` facade set with
  explicitly selected features.
- `@llama-harness/sdk` and the matching platform runtime packages use the
  managed child-sidecar protocol. The Python `llama-harness` wheel includes the
  same reviewed platform runtime.
- SDKs offer protocol 1.1 and retain the documented v1.0 fallback. They report
  their package identity in `client_hello`; the child reports its Cargo identity
  in `runtime_hello`.
- Release validation checks Cargo metadata, runtime hello, SDK tests, package
  contents, checksums, and manifest identity before any separate manual upload.

## Compatibility and upgrade

Update Rust first-party dependency constraints to `0.2.0`. Install TypeScript
or Python SDK packages only with platform runtime artifacts from the same
reviewed release. The sidecar remains private stdin/stdout JSONL; it does not
start a network service, download binaries, or own application tools and policy.

See `docs/migration.md` for migration and rollback boundaries and
`docs/releasing.md` for the manual registry sequence. This checked-in note does
not authorize publishing, tagging, or creating a release by itself.
